scenarios.name: battle_blackout
scenarios.verification: synthetic-port-gate plus real-navigation golden; state verification, not UI verification. The other half of battle_faint's coverage: battle_faint kills the ENEMY, this one kills the PLAYER, so RemoveFaintedPlayerMon and HandlePlayerBlackOut execute for the first time. Building it found a real defect: ReadPlayerMonCurHPAndStatus was a no-op, so the fainted mon's 0 HP never reached the party and the battle looped faint->resend forever

scenarios.name: trainer_battle_route
scenarios.verification: the CONTINUOUS overworld->battle->return scenario, and the only one in which the port's real OverworldLoop drives a trainer battle end to end: sight engagement by the map script, entry through the loop's own wCurOpponent poll, the live battle menus, and the .battleOccurred return that dispatches EndTrainerBattle. 44/45/46 call StartTrainerBattle and InitBattle from a harness and never run the loop, so none of them can prove this. Compared surface is choreography (battle result, wIsInBattle, wCurOpponent cleared, map-script indices, the persistent beaten flag, the .battleOccurred status-flag work, map and coords) plus the two zero-RNG reward bytes (player money BCD, lead mon EXP). Damage and HP are deliberately NOT compared: pinning them would require RNG lockstep through live menu timing, and per-turn damage math is already covered by battle_faint and 45/46
